Run it a few times on your home page and your slowest template. Over 0.8 seconds? Look at the server before the front end.

hreflang: the right page for each language.

Open one translated page and check that it links to every language version, itself included. Google ignores links…

Find the code your page never runs.

Click through the page's main task, then sort by unused bytes. Split or defer the biggest file that stays mostly red.

Myth: the padlock means the site is secure.

Check what the padlock does not cover: response headers, cookie flags, outdated scripts and a DMARC record.

SRI: a fingerprint for borrowed scripts.

List the scripts you load from other domains. Add an integrity hash to every one that has a fixed version.

The 10-minute pre-release check.

Copy the list into your release ticket and tick it on the live site, not on staging.

See your page the way Googlebot does.

Search the rendered HTML for your main heading and your key facts. If they are missing there, Google may not see them…

INP: how fast the page answers a tap.

Find the slowest tap on your page, often a menu or a filter, and break up the long task behind it.

Myth: one line of code makes a site accessible.

Spend the overlay budget on your shared templates first: header, navigation, forms and footer.

Preview colour blindness in two clicks.

Check every error message, chart and link. If colour is the only signal, add text, an icon or an underline.

Myth: a sitemap gets every page indexed.

Open the Pages report in Search Console and filter it by your sitemap. Each page left out is listed with its…

LCP: when the main thing shows up.

Open the Performance panel in Chrome DevTools: its live metrics name your LCP element. Make sure it is never lazy-loaded.

The 5-minute accessibility check.

Run all five on your home page and your busiest form. File each failure with its criterion number.

Can anyone send mail as your domain?

Run the lookup on your domain. No answer? Publish p=none with a report address, read the reports, then move to quarantine.

Skip link: jump straight past the menu.

Load your page and press Tab once. The first thing that appears should be a way to skip to the content.

Your Lighthouse score is not your visitors.

Read the top half first. If your page has no real-user data there, collect your own with Google's web-vitals…

Myth: meta keywords still help you rank.

Search your templates for name="keywords". Remove it, and write a real description for each key page instead.
